cancel_workflow.description: Stop a workflow run that is still waiting, whether in a delay step or gathering a batch. Anything already sent stays sent. Give it the same cancellation key the trigger step used.
cancel_workflow.name: cancel_workflow

parameters.description: The workflow whose run you want to stop.
parameters.name: workflow_key

parameters.description: The key the 'Trigger a workflow' step was given.
parameters.name: cancellation_key

set_object.description: Create or update a record that isn't a person: a project, a document, a repository. Objects can be subscribed to and notified just like users. Only the fields you fill in change.
set_object.name: set_object

parameters.description: The kind of record this is: Knock creates the collection the first time you write to it, so any name you use consistently works.
parameters.name: collection

parameters.description: Your own id for this record, unique within the collection.
parameters.name: object_id

parameters.description: What templates should call this record.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: A tz database name, for send windows.
parameters.name: timezone

parameters.description: A language tag such as 'en-GB'.
parameters.name: locale

parameters.description: Anything else to store on the record. These come back nested under 'properties' when you read it.

set_tenant.description: Create or update a tenant: the customer or workspace a notification belongs to. The record, its name and its custom properties work on every Knock plan; the branding fields and tenant-level preference defaults are an Enterprise feature and Knock refuses them otherwise.
set_tenant.name: set_tenant

parameters.description: Your own id for the customer or workspace. Writing to an id that doesn't exist yet creates it.
parameters.name: tenant_id

parameters.description: What to call the tenant in templates.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: icon_url, logo_url, primary_color and primary_color_contrast. Only applied on Knock's Enterprise plan: leave it blank otherwise.
parameters.name: branding

parameters.description: Anything else to store on the tenant.
parameters.name: properties

set_user_preferences.description: Write what a user does and doesn't want to be notified about, by channel type, by category or by workflow. Knock's own default replaces everything not sent, so this step defaults to merging instead: switch it to Replace only when you mean to discard the rest.
set_user_preferences.name: set_user_preferences

parameters.description: Your own id for the person, exactly as you send it to Knock. Knock stores whatever you use, so this is usually your database id.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: Merge keeps preferences this step doesn't mention. Replace discards them.
parameters.name: persistence_strategy

options.label: Merge — keep preferences this step doesn't mention
Replace — discard every preference this step doesn't send

trigger_workflow.description: Run one of your Knock workflows: Knock decides the channels, the template and the batching from what you built in the dashboard. The workflow must be committed to the environment this connection's key belongs to before the API can trigger it, in development as well as production.
trigger_workflow.name: trigger_workflow

parameters.description: The key shown under the workflow's name in Knock. Not the display name: 'new-comment', not 'New comment'.
parameters.name: workflow_key

parameters.description: Who to notify: user ids, or whole user objects to identify and notify in one step. Up to 1,000.
parameters.name: recipients

parameters.description: What the template fills itself in with: every variable your workflow references.
parameters.name: data

parameters.description: Who caused this, if anybody. A user id, or a whole user object to identify at the same time.
parameters.name: actor

parameters.description: The customer or workspace this notification belongs to. Used for per-tenant branding and preferences.
parameters.name: tenant

parameters.description: Your own id for this run, so a later 'Cancel a workflow run' step can stop it while it is still waiting in a delay or batch.
parameters.name: cancellation_key

parameters.description: Send the same key twice and Knock only runs the workflow once. Use it when a retry must not notify anybody twice.
parameters.name: idempotency_key

parameters.description: Run the workflow without actually delivering anything. Messages are still recorded.
parameters.name: sandbox_mode

parameters.description: Run the workflow's delay steps through immediately.
parameters.name: skip_delay

description: Send the notifications you designed in Knock from a workflow: trigger a workflow by key for up to a thousand recipients at once, with the data its templates fill themselves in from. Keep the people and records Knock notifies up to date, read and write their channel and category preferences, group them by tenant, and look back over everything that was sent and what the recipients did with it.
